trickyParts: The seed's history versions change exactly the real sizes: padding is a stream of unique words grown or cut by the size change; typed ask answers and resolves land at their real version numbers; 21 versions on 10 typed-ask documents keep |delta| with the sign flipped.

Dispatch 35efd326 matches an edit's find against rendered text inside one block; replay_edit.go builds only plain one-line runs; TestReplayEditsBundle checks all 1,003 window edits and 1,490 anchor quotes offline.
Dispatch mints a new id for each block an edit creates, so the end-state digest names a block by its position.

A newer build renders some markdown differently (a pipe in a table cell's code span): the client reads each modelled document's text from the build before the window and replans only documents that differ.
Dispatch caps a JSON body at 1 MiB: padding edits send only their change; TestRequestBodiesBundle holds every planned body under the cap.
To restart from the evidence: source an env file with LOADTEST_ROOT and the 7 port variables per command; never export them into a persistent shell (a stale export once rebuilt the wrong root).
deviations: Seed dump compression is gzip 9: pgserver's Postgres 16.2 pg_dump has no zstd.
Default F is 0.05, not chosen among 0.05/0.1/0.15 by a run at 0.05 alone: 0.1 and 0.15 saturated, so 0.05 is the largest unsaturated; the three baselines are the F 0.05 runs.

The acceptance-4 baselines ran at head 5ff16983; later commits changed the end-state digest, the dashboard client (main removed SSE) and the client's start text, not the CPU measurement; head-35b at 4b756a26 repeats a 10-minute window at 9.33 cores with the same end state as earlier runs.
Main's #2449 removed GET /api/v1/events; the replay opens SSE streams for builds without /ws/live (35efd326) and live sockets otherwise, recorded as config.dashboard.
openQuestions: The upload share U moves the result non-monotonically (U 0: 13.1, U 0.25: 9.8, U 0.5: 15.9 cores), because uploads orphan anchors; whether production's named versions were uploads or edits is unknown and decides the absolute figure. Sent to the INFRA-512 architect with the report.
discoveredComplexity: At 35efd326 a 500 KB upload can take 47-60 s on 2 cores; one 10-minute run (head-35) had one upload pass its 60 s deadline and was flagged saturated; the rerun (head-35b) had none.
